stem: Sneha uses a circuit tester with a bulb to check aluminium and copper. Which claim is correct?

options.text: Aluminium makes the bulb glow, so aluminium is a good conductor.
Aluminium leaves the bulb off when a tester wire is disconnected, so aluminium does not conduct.
A glowing bulb means the material is a poor conductor.
Dull copper is a poor conductor.

teacher.key_rationale: Glow in a complete tester circuit means the material conducts. A disconnected wire blocks glow without proving the material fails. Glow does not mean poor conduction. Shininess does not decide conductivity.
